description: Etiquettes that nurture presence of heart before, during, and after the prayer.

entries.title: Make wudu with presence
entries.explanation: Begin wudu with the name of Allah, washing each limb with attention — each drop carries away sins as the Prophet ﷺ described.
entries.citation: When a Muslim performs wudu, every sin his eyes saw falls away with the water. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Walk to the prayer calmly
entries.explanation: Do not rush. Dignity and tranquility on the way to salah are themselves worship; complete what you miss afterward.
entries.citation: When the prayer is called, walk to it with calmness and dignity, and do not run. — Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim

entries.title: Straighten and close the rows
entries.explanation: Shoulder to shoulder, foot to foot — the Prophet ﷺ warned that gaps in rows invite discord between hearts.
entries.citation: Straighten your rows, for straightening them is part of establishing the prayer. — Sahih al-Bukhari

entries.title: Focus the gaze at the place of sujud
entries.explanation: Keep eyes lowered and fixed at the spot of prostration; turning the gaze away is 'the snatching of Shaytan' from prayer.
entries.citation: Let a man beware, for the Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah does not cease turning His face toward His servant in prayer, so long as the servant does not turn away.' — Sunan Abu Dawud

entries.title: Recite with tartil and reflection
entries.explanation: Do not hurry. Feel what you say; the Prophet ﷺ paused at every verse of Surah al-Fatihah.
entries.citation: Recite the Qur'an in a measured, rhythmic tone. — Qur'an 73:4

entries.title: Pause in each posture
entries.explanation: Complete ruku and sujud; the one who does not is 'the worst thief — who steals from his prayer.'
entries.citation: The worst thief among people is the one who steals from his prayer — by not completing his ruku and sujud. — Musnad Ahmad (sahih)

entries.title: Avoid fidgeting and looking around
entries.explanation: Still hands, still eyes — remember you are speaking to the King of kings.
entries.citation: Do not lift your gaze to the sky lest your sight be snatched away. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Sit briefly after the prayer for dhikr
entries.explanation: Do not leap up. Say astaghfirullah three times, then the ma'thur adhkar; angels pray for you as long as you stay.
entries.citation: The angels keep praying for one of you as long as he is in his place of prayer. — Sahih al-Bukhari

entries.title: Do not pray while holding in restroom needs
entries.explanation: Do not begin prayer while food is served or while holding urine — both distract from khushu.
entries.citation: No prayer when food is served, nor while holding in urine or stool. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Pray the sunan of fajr and the witr
entries.explanation: The two rak'ah of fajr are 'better than the world and all it contains.' Witr is the final worship of the night.
entries.citation: The two rak'ah of fajr are better than the world and all it contains. — Sahih Muslim

description: Respect for the houses of Allah.

entries.title: Enter with the right foot
entries.explanation: Step in with the right foot reciting the dua of entry; the left foot leads when leaving.
entries.citation: When any of you enters the mosque, let him say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Pray two rak'ah of tahiyyat al-masjid
entries.explanation: Do not sit until you have prayed two rak'ah greeting the mosque — unless the congregation has already begun.
entries.citation: When any of you enters the mosque, let him not sit until he has prayed two rak'ah. — Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim

entries.title: Keep the mosque clean and quiet
entries.explanation: Remove anything that harms the place of worship. Do not raise your voice; do not conduct worldly business there.
entries.citation: He who hears a person asking about a lost item in the mosque should say: 'May Allah not return it to you,' for the mosques were not built for this. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Do not step over shoulders
entries.explanation: Come early and find your row. Crossing over worshippers on Jumu'ah is rebuked in clear hadith.
entries.citation: Sit down; you have harmed people and come late. — Sunan Abu Dawud (sahih)

description: Reverence toward the Book of Allah.

entries.title: Begin with taʿawwudh and basmalah
entries.explanation: Seek refuge with Allah before reciting, and begin each surah (except Surah at-Tawbah) with the basmalah.
entries.citation: When you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from the outcast Shaytan. — Qur'an 16:98

entries.title: Be in a state of purity and dignity
entries.explanation: Touch the mushaf with wudu; sit facing qiblah if possible; keep it above other books.
entries.citation: None shall touch it except the purified. — Qur'an 56:79

entries.title: Recite slowly with reflection
entries.explanation: A short portion read with reflection is better than racing through many pages.
entries.citation: Recite the Qur'an in a measured, rhythmic tone. — Qur'an 73:4

entries.title: Act on what you learn
entries.explanation: The Qur'an is either proof for you or against you. Internalize one command each reading and try to live it.
entries.citation: Will they then not reflect on the Qur'an, or are there locks upon their hearts? — Qur'an 47:24

entries.title: Speak kindly or keep silent
entries.explanation: Speech has weight; every word is recorded by a watcher. Better to stay silent than to wound or sin.
entries.citation: Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent. — Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim

entries.title: Avoid backbiting and gossip
entries.explanation: Backbiting is mentioning your brother in a way he would dislike, even if true. Qur'an likens it to eating his dead flesh.
entries.citation: Would any of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother? You would detest it. — Qur'an 49:12

entries.title: Avoid lying, even in jest
entries.explanation: Truthfulness leads to righteousness; lying leads to sin. The Prophet ﷺ warned against lying to make people laugh.
entries.citation: Woe to the one who speaks, lying to make people laugh. Woe to him, woe to him. — Sunan Abu Dawud (sahih)

entries.title: Avoid suspicion and spying
entries.explanation: Refrain from assuming evil of others without clear evidence; much suspicion is sin.
entries.citation: O you who believe, avoid much suspicion, for some suspicion is sin. — Qur'an 49:12

entries.title: Do not argue even if right
entries.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ guaranteed a house in the highest part of Paradise for the one who abandons argumentation even when in the right.
entries.citation: I guarantee a house in the highest part of Paradise for one who leaves arguing even if he is right. — Sunan Abu Dawud (sahih)

description: Birr al-walidayn — the duty to parents.

entries.title: Honor and obey in the permissible
entries.explanation: Obey their good instructions; serve them with patience, especially in old age.
entries.citation: Your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment... — Qur'an 17:23

entries.title: Lower the wing of humility
entries.explanation: Do not sigh, raise your voice, or walk ahead of them rudely. Soft words and mercy outweigh heavy service.
entries.citation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy... — Qur'an 17:24

entries.title: Make dua for them, alive or dead
entries.explanation: A righteous child's dua reaches the deceased; the mother's supplication is answered for the living.
entries.citation: Rabbi irhamhumā kamā rabbayānī ṣaghīrā. — Qur'an 17:24

entries.title: Maintain their ties and friends
entries.explanation: After their death, keep their relatives and friends — part of the highest birr.
entries.citation: The best kind of righteousness is for a man to maintain relations with his father's friends after he has died. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Be gentle with your spouse
entries.explanation: The best of you is the best to his family; strength is shown in kindness, not control.
entries.citation: The best of you are those who are best to their wives. — Sunan at-Tirmidhi (sahih)

entries.title: Play with and teach your children
entries.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ carried his grandchildren in sujud and smiled at them; raise them with love and discipline, not fear only.
entries.citation: He is not of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect to our elders. — Sunan at-Tirmidhi (sahih)

entries.title: Keep family secrets
entries.explanation: What happens in private between spouses is an amanah; exposing it is betrayal.
entries.citation: The worst of people before Allah on the Day of Judgment is a man who is intimate with his wife, then spreads her secrets. — Sahih Muslim

description: Adab of the student and the scholar.

entries.title: Begin with intention
entries.explanation: Seek knowledge sincerely to benefit yourself and others, not merely for reputation or degrees.
entries.citation: Whoever seeks knowledge to contend with scholars or to argue with fools... Allah will enter him into the Fire. — Sunan at-Tirmidhi (sahih)

entries.title: Be consistent
entries.explanation: Small, regular steps in learning are more lasting than bursts that fade.
entries.citation: The most beloved deeds to Allah are those done consistently, even if small. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Honor your teacher
entries.explanation: Humility before a teacher opens the heart to knowledge; arrogance closes it.
entries.citation: He is not of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect to our elders and scholars. — Sunan at-Tirmidhi

entries.title: Act on what you learn
entries.explanation: Knowledge without action is a burden; the righteous scholars lived what they taught.
entries.citation: Whoever acts upon what he knows, Allah will cause him to inherit knowledge of what he did not know. — Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah

entries.title: Say Bismillah at the start
entries.explanation: If you forgot, say: Bismillahi awwalahu wa akhirahu. Eat with the right hand, from what is in front of you.
entries.citation: O boy, say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is near you. — Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim

entries.title: Avoid over-eating
entries.explanation: A third for food, a third for drink, a third for breath. No container is worse than a full stomach.
entries.citation: The son of Adam fills no container worse than his stomach. — Sunan at-Tirmidhi (sahih)

entries.title: Do not criticize food
entries.explanation: If you like it, eat; if not, leave it without complaint.
entries.citation: The Prophet ﷺ never criticized food. If he liked it he ate; if not, he left it. — Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim

entries.title: Eat together and share
entries.explanation: Blessing descends on food eaten together. Do not turn away a beggar or friend empty-handed.
entries.citation: Eat together and do not eat separately, for the blessing is in congregation. — Sunan Ibn Majah (sahih)

entries.title: Say al-hamdu lillah when done
entries.explanation: Praise follows every bounty; the simplest dua after eating brings forgiveness.
entries.citation: Whoever eats food and says 'Al-hamdu lillah...' his past sins are forgiven. — Sunan Abu Dawud (sahih)

entries.title: Spread salam generously
entries.explanation: To one you know and one you do not. Salam is the greeting of Paradise; it plants love between hearts.
entries.citation: Shall I tell you of something that will make you love one another? Spread salam. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Shake hands and smile
entries.explanation: A smile in your brother's face is charity; handshakes cause sins to fall.
entries.citation: No two Muslims meet and shake hands except that they are forgiven before they part. — Sunan Abu Dawud (sahih)

entries.title: Do not whisper when three are sitting
entries.explanation: Do not pair off in whispers while a third is present — it grieves them.
entries.citation: When you are three, do not let two converse in secret apart from the third. — Sahih al-Bukhari & Muslim

entries.title: Make space for newcomers
entries.explanation: Shift and widen the circle; Allah will widen mercy for you.
entries.citation: When you are told to make room in assemblies, make room — Allah will make room for you. — Qur'an 58:11

entries.title: Recite the travel dua
entries.explanation: Subhan alladhi sakhara lana hadha wa ma kunna lahu muqrineen... Reminds you that the vehicle is from Allah.
entries.citation: When the Prophet ﷺ settled on his mount to travel, he would say Allahu Akbar three times, then recite it. — Sahih Muslim

entries.title: Leave before dawn when possible
entries.explanation: Travel early; blessing is placed in the early hours of the day.
entries.citation: O Allah, bless my ummah in its early morning. — Sunan at-Tirmidhi (sahih)

entries.title: The traveller's dua is answered
entries.explanation: Three duas are never refused: the oppressed, the traveller, and the parent for the child. Use the journey to pray.
entries.citation: Three duas are answered with no doubt: the oppressed, the traveller, the parent for his child. — Sunan Abu Dawud (sahih)

entries.title: Sleep on your right side
entries.explanation: Dust the bed, lie on the right side, place right hand under the cheek — the sunnah posture of the Prophet ﷺ.
entries.citation: When the Prophet ﷺ wished to sleep, he would lie on his right side. — Sahih al-Bukhari

entries.title: Recite the three quls, Ayat al-Kursi, and bismillah
entries.explanation: Blow into your palms, wipe over yourself; Ayat al-Kursi keeps a guardian with you till morning.
entries.citation: Whoever reads Ayat al-Kursi before sleeping, Allah appoints a guardian over him. — Sahih al-Bukhari

entries.title: End with the last dua of the night
entries.explanation: Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya — to die in the remembrance of Allah is to live it.
entries.citation: The Prophet ﷺ said this as he lay down to sleep. — Sahih al-Bukhari
